title: Composition for bounded constructible compact support with all adic coefficients
statement: Fix a universe u, a prime ell and a field k of positive characteristic different from ell. All schemes are separated finite-type k-schemes in u. Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring with a certificate IsEllAdicCoefficient ell Lambda, allowing continuous finite extensions, integral valuation rings with torsion, and the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate]. Write B_T for the full bounded constructible subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal Lambda_T-module objects [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible; sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For composable k-morphisms f:X -> Y and g:Y -> S there is a natural isomorphism of functors B_X -> B_S between boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Lambda ell (f;g) and boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Lambda ell f followed by boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Lambda ell g. These are the recorded compactification-based restrictions of ordinary compact-support direct image. The redundant IsFinitenessCoefficient instance in the Lean signature is deduced from the adic certificate. The assertion includes integral valuation-ring coefficients and their torsion complexes.

proof.text: For integral coefficients install the norm induced by the given embedding in the algebraic closure. Derived finite reduction makes the proper exchange invertible, and integral reduction conservativity detects the isomorphism. Normalize the coefficient to integralCoeff before constructing the exchange component. For the two rational coefficient constructors use the existing proper-base-change theorems.

The open-extension base-change isomorphism yields the exchange mate. Its restriction to the open is invertible by full faithfulness of both extension adjunctions. On the closed complement, proper base change identifies the target with a pushforward of a vanishing restriction. Open/closed joint conservativity makes the mate invertible. Reuse sharedBoundedOpenUnitIsIso from the already imported ExchangeMono module for both bounded open adjunction units; do not restate the existing bounded-unit theorem.

The existing generic refinement-pushforward argument and these proper exchange isomorphisms compare compactifications along common refinements. Take the cartesian compactification of the proper half of f followed by the open half of g. Compactification independence, composition of open extension and proper direct images, and inverse exchange give the claimed isomorphism. All choices of refinements are eliminated in theorem proofs; no data definition chooses a witness of an unproved mere existence.

For the later closed-support application, also prove the private proper comparison: the explicit compactification with identity open part and proper part f gives Rf! ~= Rf_*. The identity open extension is identified with the identity by uniqueness of adjoints. Exact closed pushforward identifies its right derivation with levelwise derivation.

    Nonempty (boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Λ ℓ (f ≫ g) ≅
      boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Λ ℓ f ⋙ boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Λ ℓ g)
